**Example material · Synthetic observations · 18 October 2026**

## The shape is only half the evidence

A polished chart compresses many decisions into a small space. Which observations were collected, which were excluded and which never existed all shape its meaning.

Our fictional series records a monthly count at a small service desk. The modest range is deliberate: it lets readers inspect exact values in the chart table rather than interpreting decorative volatility.

```chart
type: line
title: "Observed requests"
data:
  inline:
    - {category: "May", value: 41}
    - {category: "Jun", value: 45}
    - {category: "Jul", value: 43}
    - {category: "Aug", value: 48}
    - {category: "Sep", value: 46}
    - {category: "Oct", value: 49}
encoding: {x: category, y: value}
axes:
  x: {label: Category}
  y: {label: "Observed requests"}
```

*Source: Synthetic example, authored on 18 October 2026. No real customers or service desk are represented.*

## What to take away

A responsible update would add new observations and retain the definition of a request. It would not quietly rewrite earlier counts to make the trend look more persuasive.
